maxImageEdge.note: maxImageEdge is a DSH-only downscale. CW-15 introduced it on the Python/plugin surface; D-E was later revised so it also reaches the desktop Rust path, because the measured pain was a full-resolution 1920x1200 desktop screenshot and the built-in 1920 default never bit (1200 < 1920). It is still never applied by default: 0 or unset changes nothing on any path, and the plugin only exports DSH_COMPUTER_USE_MAX_IMAGE_EDGE when the user explicitly configures a finite positive value. Desktop screenshots still undergo the official DPI normalisation above; 0 = disabled = official behaviour; a positive value is opt-in token saving.

windowFilter.dshHostFrameClassesNote: CW-4 DSH addition: the UWP frame window is owned by ApplicationFrameHost.exe and carries no app identity. ApplicationFrameWindow is a Windows shell class with no literal in the official binary, so official reaches the real app through the child Windows.UI.Core.CoreWindow. Treating the frame class the same way is what keeps ApplicationFrameHost.exe out of list_windows.

cursorMotion.source: Measured against the official helper on 2026-09-14: full-screen ULW layer CodexComputerUseCursorOverlay, PrintWindow centroid at ~30 Hz, resolution +/-40 ms. See analysis/deep-dive/11-official-sampling.md section 3. These settle times are externally observed, not binary constants.
cursorMotion.singleSourceOfTruth: helper-rs/src/overlay/motion.rs consts; the Rust test cursor_motion_constants_match_the_single_source fails on any drift in either direction.
cursorMotion.binaryShortDurationNote: 14004b7e8 single-segment literal. Refuted for the observable settle: L=80/120/180 px measure 304-383 ms, and 0.34 s (singleSegmentDurationS) lands inside every +/-40 ms window. Kept for provenance only.
cursorMotion.binaryBowAxisNote: Fixed 46-degree screen axis in the binary (14004b7e8:364-369). The measured trajectories bow perpendicular to the chord, so the axis is retained as provenance; the empirical bow above builds the path.
cursorMotion.binaryDurationPolynomialNote: 14004b7e8:556-636. Refuted by the measured settle (25-63% short for L>=269 px, and monotone where the official is not); Rust keeps it as binary_duration_polynomial_s for provenance, plan() uses the measured curve.

samples.label: d0
samples.note: no translation (snap); the 218 ms centroid pulse is the press animation, whose official Scale keyframe is the separate 550 ms constant

cursorMotion.knownLimit: The internal law could not be separated from 10 samples: the measured settle is non-monotone in L (400->691 ms, 613->678 ms; 760->786 ms, 998->651 ms). The model keys on the externally observable chord law plus a diagonal-shortening term; it does not claim the binary's internal parameterisation.

deviations.owner: DSH-specific choices that intentionally differ from the official binary. Every entry needs a reason and must not be presented as parity.
deviations.framePoolBuffersReason: The arrival handler parks the newest frame in `latest`; with a single buffer the pool could not produce the next frame, so every screenshot froze on the first composition. Behaviour (encode the newest frame) matches official; only the buffer count differs.
deviations.gdiFallbackReason: Official is WGC-only and fails loudly. DSH keeps GDI fallbacks for availability and surfaces the chosen path in captureState.path so the model can tell a frame may not reflect occlusion.
deviations.maxImageEdgeReason: Never applied by default, on any path: 0 or unset is the official no-cap behaviour (decision D-E, revised -- it previously read "must never be applied to the desktop Rust path"). It reaches the desktop Rust path only when the user explicitly configures maxImageEdge > 0, which the plugin carries as the DSH_COMPUTER_USE_MAX_IMAGE_EDGE environment variable because the official helper's argv parser rejects unknown flags.
